svg.title: Shadewright executor
svg.desc: Zoom into the executor identity. A RemediationRequest passes, in order: the policy engine's field checks on the request, policy, settings and live target (a refusal costs no Git read and no token), the source mapping (Flux objects to the one file in Git, within an input budget), the full policy decision (policy, settings, live target state and the resolved source), the limits (concurrency, a lock per target, a circuit breaker with one probe when half-open; only an allowed request is held back as Queued and checked again every 30 seconds, or every 10 minutes behind a lock held by a request that stopped, a refusal is never held back; with --verify-outcomes on, a merged request keeps the lock on its target until it ends, and a request queued behind it for the same field ends Superseded when it ends Succeeded), the freshness check, the patcher with the semantic diff, and the kill switch gate, which reads spec.paused right before every Git write. The Key Vault signer signs for the GitHub App, which creates the branch, commit and pull request outside the cluster; the request waits in AwaitingApproval. When a person merges, the controller observes the merge and the request reaches Merged with its merge receipt, which is also the breaker's success. With the flag --verify-outcomes (off by default) it then waits in WaitingForDelivery until the Flux Kustomization reports the receipt's merge commit, or a later commit that holds it, applied (Delivered), and is checked in Verifying from the executor's own reads (Configured, RolledOut, the template recorded) and the verifier's report, read with get as untrusted evidence; it ends Succeeded with Cleared True after a quiet window, Failed or Inconclusive, never Expired, and reports only, never acting on pods. Refusals end in Denied, NeedsIntervention or Superseded. Built and not drawn: a revert (spec.reverts) has its link to the failed request checked before the policy engine's field checks (otherwise Denied with InvalidRevert), always needs a person's approval, reads no verifier report and ends Inconclusive with RevertApplied, never Succeeded. The analyzer proposes such a revert, once per failed request (built, not drawn: it is not the executor). Planned and not drawn: auto-merge. Where a request ends: a refused field check or policy decision ends Denied, an unmappable source ends NeedsIntervention, and a stale plan ends Superseded; the freshness check rechecks the plan inputs every 5 minutes. The patcher allows only the one field change (any other change ends NeedsIntervention). The Key Vault signer signs the GitHub App JWT with RS256 and the key stays in the vault; the App works on one repository and on shadewright/* branches. The kill switch gate reads spec.paused right before every Git write, and a paused or unreadable setting means no write. After verification a request ends Succeeded, Failed or Inconclusive. svg.text: Ends: Denied, NeedsIntervention, Superseded (refused). Succeeded, Failed, Inconclusive (verified).
Teal: outside the cluster. Verifying runs only with the flag, which is off by default.
